title: PCSX2's shader notice now says how much work actually finished
summary: The overlay replaces a vague compiling message with the number of shaders and total milliseconds, using one cleaned-up indicator across Metal, Vulkan, OpenGL, Direct3D 11, and Direct3D 12.
heroAlt: Source evidence from PCSX2 pull request #14450: GS: Track shader compile count and duration for OSD

sourceLabels.pcsx2-pr-14450: GS: Track shader compile count and duration for OSD

blocks.text: Compiling Shaders explained a pause without measuring it

When a game or renderer encounters uncached pipelines, PCSX2 can spend visible time compiling shaders. The old overlay confirmed that compilation was happening but not whether it involved two shaders or hundreds, nor whether the work lasted a few milliseconds or a major startup stall. That leaves performance reports dependent on perception and makes it difficult to compare cache or backend behavior.
One indicator accumulates count and wall-clock duration

Pull request #14450 cleans GSShaderCompileIndicator and changes the final message to Compiled x shaders in y ms. The count identifies the size of the burst, while duration captures its immediate cost. An erroneous ScopedCompilation use in GSMTLDeviceInfo is removed so Metal follows the intended common lifecycle instead of applying an extra scope that could distort indicator state.
The result is reported after work and still fades normally

The overlay remains tied to the existing GPU-usage display behavior and fades out after reporting the completed burst. It is diagnostic, not a persistent benchmark panel. The author tested Metal, Vulkan, OpenGL, Direct3D 12, and Direct3D 11, important because each backend creates different pipeline objects while the user should see one consistent message format.
Cold and warm cache runs should tell different stories

Delete the shader cache or launch an unplayed game with the relevant OSD option enabled, then record the count, milliseconds, and fade behavior. Revisit the same scene with a warm cache and expect a smaller or absent burst. Test backend switching, concurrent compilation, pause, and shutdown while the indicator is active. Compare reported duration with trace timing, but do not treat it as total frame-stutter time because other pipeline and I/O work can overlap.
The message is now evidence: a shader count and elapsed time can be compared, reported, and tied to a cold-cache event.
